positioning.promise: Low-priced cross-border marketplace for goods mostly shipped from China, with a curated 'Choice' tier that adds free shipping above a low threshold, delivery commitments, and free returns in selected countries.

features.capability: Large third-party seller marketplace for inexpensive goods from China, bought through the mobile app
Choice items: free shipping on orders over $10 or of three or more items in most markets
Free doorstep delivery to Israel on orders over $45 (report undated; current status unverified)
China-to-Israel delivery reported at about one week to 10 days; Israeli warehouses allow faster delivery for stocked items
Israeli last-mile logistics arm (Parcel Home), launched 2024, with about 45 distribution points as of April 2026
Israeli-registered businesses can sell directly to Israeli shoppers on AliExpress, with faster domestic shipping for electronics, appliances, and e-bikes
Buyer Protection: disputes or refunds for non-delivery within the guaranteed window or for items not as described or damaged (about 15 days after receipt, per guides that disagree on the window)
Choice delivery guarantee in Israel: refund if an order is lost or not delivered after 45 days (reported, undated)
US: $1 coupon for a missed Choice delivery date; first return per parent order free; returns start within 90 days of payment
Dispute and customer-service experience: users report bot-only support, being charged return postage for wrong or faulty items, and difficulty disputing misleading listings
Listing trust: users report fake 5-star reviews, misleading photos and descriptions, and scam shops
App usability: users report a cluttered UI, confusing games and coins, navigation that jumps to the home page, slowdowns, and a cart that fails to accept items
Dropshipping Center: free in-account tool for product research, supplier vetting, and volume-based dropshipper tiers
AliExpress Open Platform: Basic APIs open to all business types; Value-Added APIs need an AliExpress-approved application, under an API Use Agreement last updated January 2022
Dropshipper order placement and logistics-tracking endpoints (about 185 endpoints overall, with no official OpenAPI spec)
Israeli customer club (loyalty program), reportedly launched alongside expectations of more than 20 million packages a month
Hebrew/RTL interface and ILS checkout in the app and web store

distribution.claim: Google Play shows 16,287,667 ratings, with storefront ratings of 4.56 (il), 4.24 (us), and 4.18 (gb); the app is free.
AliExpress, Temu, and Shein account for about 75% of Israelis' online orders, against about 6% for Amazon (Shop Analytics, mid-2026).
About 52.8 million packages arrived in Israel from overseas websites in 2025, covering all platforms, not only AliExpress.
AliExpress uses Singles' Day launches, an Israeli customer club, and frequent coverage in Israeli consumer news as acquisition surfaces.
KSP led Israeli local sites in June 2026 with 18% of orders among the top 20 local sites, making it the main local substitute signal found.

release_signals.claim: Frequent app releases: reviews cite version 8.115.1 (Dec 2024), 8.129.11 (Jun 2025), 8.173.3 (Sep 2026), 8.177.3, and 8.180.1 (Nov 2026).
Choice launched in March 2023 with free shipping, free returns, and delivery guarantees in selected countries.
Israel build-out timeline: Airport City warehouse pilot (2022), Parcel Home logistics arm (2024), and Israeli sellers opened before Singles' Day (exact date not confirmed, likely late 2025).
A 2026 app redesign is suggested by a Nov 2026 review complaining that navigation changed.

dependencies.claim: Israball's automated sourcing depends on AliExpress Open Platform terms; Value-Added APIs (likely including dropshipper order placement) need AliExpress approval and can be revoked under the agreement.
Israeli landed cost depends on the volatile personal-import VAT exemption, now $75 with 18% VAT above it.
Delivery speed to Israel depends on AliExpress logistics (Israeli warehouses, Parcel Home) and on regional security conditions.
Product quality and listing accuracy depend on third-party AliExpress sellers that users report as inconsistent.

risks.claim: AliExpress is closing the speed gap in Israel itself (local warehouses, Parcel Home, Israeli sellers), which erodes a 'faster than AliExpress' angle for Israball.

Inference: shoppers can find the same item on AliExpress, so any Israball markup is easy to expose; differentiation has to come from curation, Hebrew service, and recourse rather than access to products.
Price ceiling pressure: Temu is positioned in Israel as cheaper than AliExpress, and users describe AliExpress prices as rising.
Policy volatility: the VAT exemption changed three times between Dec 2025 and mid-2026 under local-retailer lobbying.
Geopolitical shocks cut cross-border orders sharply: in March 2026, Amazon orders fell 75% and Temu 68% as Israelis shifted to local sites.
Inference: when Israball dropships, Buyer Protection disputes belong to Israball as the AliExpress buyer, so Israball absorbs refund and return costs that users already report as painful.
AliExpress's earlier local presence in Israel faded by late 2021, a signal that local-presence initiatives can be withdrawn.

contradictions.claim: Israeli delivery times conflict: a 3-7 business-day target (2022 warehouse pilot), about a week to 10 days from China (Ynet), and 7-10 days via local warehouses (Globes 2026).
VAT-exemption sources conflict ($150 effective Dec 23, 2025; $130 reissued Feb 2026; $75 restored). The latest evidence points to $75 since about late June 2026.
Choice free-return caps differ by source (first return per order, up to 5 per month, up to 3 per month), as do covered country counts.
Israel free-shipping thresholds differ: $45 doorstep delivery versus $10 for Choice items.
Store ratings differ by storefront (il 4.56 vs gb 4.18), but 71 of 75 sampled reviews appeared in multiple markets, so the review sample is not market-specific.

unknowns.claim: Official AliExpress, Alibaba Group, and Ynet pages could not be fetched (hosts outside the session's allowed network), so all official claims come from search-result snippets and stay unverified.
Current Choice terms for Israel are unknown: free-return availability, delivery-guarantee window, and late-delivery compensation.
The date and current validity of the $45 Israel free doorstep-delivery threshold are unknown.
Whether the AliExpress app and web store offer Hebrew/RTL and ILS checkout is unknown.
Current Dropshipping Center and Open Platform terms are unknown, including whether dropship orders to Israeli addresses support neutral or unbranded packaging and Israeli logistics options.
No price anchors were collected for candidate niches (sports gear, home gadgets, pet supplies) on AliExpress, Temu, Shein, or Israeli retailers.
No current delivery terms were collected for Israeli local substitutes (Ivory, Zap, Wallashops, KSP delivery SLAs) or for Temu/Shein in Israel.
The official Buyer Protection dispute window and coverage rules are not confirmed on an AliExpress-controlled page.
GB market web evidence was not gathered beyond store metadata; US evidence is limited to store metadata and one press release.
